dash.name: Prism operations
dash.testLine: This copy is for testing deploys. The dashboard people use is Prism operations.
dash.warehouse: These tiles read Prism's tables through the SQL warehouse. If they are blank at first, the warehouse is starting, which can take up to a minute.
dash.note: I give no percentage, median, rate per 100 or range from fewer than {fewest} cases. Where a tile has fewer, it shows the count instead.

findings.title: What the measures say

dates.title: Dates

readiness.source: Prism's data readiness measures in strata.ops.

gov.intro: This page shows whether each nightly run passed its quality checks, what Azure has cost against the budget, and what personal data I removed at ingestion. It also shows who read Prism's tables, and traces any answer back through its tool calls to its sources.
gov.source: Prism's pipeline runs, quality checks, agent runs and Azure cost records in strata.ops, and the workspace's query history where Free Edition shows it.

budgetPeriod.title: Budget period
budgetPeriod.about: The free credit, then each month after it, newest first. It sets the Azure spend tiles.

runId.title: Run ID
runId.about: Empty means the latest answer run. Paste a run ID from Recent answer runs to see that run.

sections.runsText: Each night the job takes in only what changed and checks row counts, missing keys, missing Disclosed dates and duplicate rows. The chart shows the last run of each night.
sections.spendText: Azure budgets only send alerts. The limits come from caps: a tokens-per-minute limit on each model deployment, a daily page cap on reading documents, and at most two copies of anything hosted.
sections.queriesText: Prism's app runs every query as the person using it, so their name appears here, not the app's.
sections.lineage: Lineage from an answer to its sources
sections.lineageText: Leave Run ID empty to see the latest answer, or paste a run ID from Recent answer runs, at the end of this section. If the tables stay empty, no answer run has that ID.

gov.removeWhy: I remove the contact person's name, email address and phone number from every procurement notice as I take it in, before it reaches any table that answers or this dashboard can read. Prism never shows them and never answers questions about them. The counter above counts any email addresses, phone numbers and names after "Attention" that got through.
gov.noHistory: I can't show who queried what, because this workspace doesn't let me read its query history. I checked when this dashboard was deployed on {date}. If Free Edition adds it later, deploying the dashboard again adds the table here.

ai.intro: This page shows how my answers did on the benchmark, in Microsoft Foundry's evaluations and in my own six checks. It also shows the leading and lagging indicators of the knowledge, retrieval and estimates loops, and how people used Prism. Each tile's description defines its measure.
ai.source: Prism's evaluation results, agent runs, feedback, lesson decisions, exposure logs, usage events and draft states in strata.ops.

sections.answersText: How my answers did on the benchmark, in Microsoft Foundry's evaluations and in my own six checks.
sections.loopsText: Each loop has a leading indicator, which moves first, and a lagging indicator, which confirms it later. Lessons are decided weekly, search is tuned at most monthly, and the time estimate model is retrained quarterly.
sections.adoptionText: Who used Prism, which drafts their authors finished, and how often a plan row was dated within 14 days of a date I offered.

ai.abbreviations: Implementation Completion and Results Report (ICR), Project Performance Assessment Report (PPAR), normalized discounted cumulative gain at 10 (nDCG at 10). ICR Review is the World Bank's own name.

checks_failed.name: Quality checks failed in the latest nightly run
checks_failed.definition: Checks of row counts, missing keys, missing Disclosed dates and duplicate rows, run by each task of the nightly job. The latest run in the dates chosen above.
checks_failed.outof: Out of the checks that run ran. The table of nightly runs gives the total.

azure_spend.name: Azure spend this budget period
azure_spend.definition: Azure charges from the daily cost pull, against the budget for the period chosen above. Azure budgets only send alerts, so the caps set the limit.
azure_spend.outof: Out of the budget for that period. The table of spend by day gives the running total.

contacts_left.name: Notices still carrying contact details
contacts_left.definition: Procurement notices in which the latest check found an email address or a phone number. I remove them at ingestion, so this count should be zero.
contacts_left.outof: Out of the procurement notices that check read.

benchmark_passed.name: Benchmark questions passed
benchmark_passed.definition: Benchmark questions that met their expected answer, citations, range or refusal. The latest full gate run in the dates chosen above.
benchmark_passed.outof: Out of the questions in the latest full gate run. The table under Answers gives the total.

sentences_removed.name: Sentences the verifier removed
sentences_removed.definition: Sentences in answers that failed one of my six checks, out of all the sentences I wrote in answers. In the dates chosen above.
sentences_removed.outof: Out of the sentences I wrote. The table of reasons gives the total.

answers_held_back.name: Answers where I held back
answers_held_back.definition: Answers in which I gave no range, time estimate or share because the evidence fell short, out of all answers, refusals included. In the dates chosen above.
answers_held_back.outof: Out of the answers I gave. The table of reasons gives the total.

weekly_users.name: Weekly users
weekly_users.definition: People who opened at least one page of Prism in the last full week in the dates chosen above, Monday to Sunday. Each person counts once, whatever view they used.
weekly_users.outof: A count of people, with no total.

drafts_exported.name: Drafts exported
drafts_exported.definition: Drafts started in the dates chosen above that their authors marked as checked and then exported. Only a draft's author can do either.
drafts_exported.outof: Out of the drafts started. The table of use by week gives the total.

plan_rows_offered.name: Plan rows dated within 14 days of a date I offered
plan_rows_offered.definition: Plan rows published after I showed a past range or time estimate for their package, whose planned signing date fell within 14 days of a date I offered. In the dates chosen above.
plan_rows_offered.outof: Out of the plan rows published after I showed a range. The table of plan rows by month gives the total.

days_to_decision.name: Days from publication to decision
days_to_decision.definition: Calendar days from the day an Implementation Completion and Results Report (ICR), ICR Review or Project Performance Assessment Report (PPAR) was published to the day a lead procurement specialist decided on a lesson proposed from it. The target is a decision within 10 business days.
days_to_decision.outof: Out of the proposed lessons decided.

blamed_covered.name: Blamed risks a lesson covered at approval
blamed_covered.definition: In the hindsight test, the risks that completion reports later blamed, and how many of them a lesson in my library already covered on the project's approval date.
blamed_covered.outof: Out of the risks completion reports blamed.

wrong_passage_rate.name: Wrong-passage reports per 100 sources opened
wrong_passage_rate.definition: How many passages people marked as wrong for every 100 sources they opened from an answer. Reports sent in a preview, and reports that were withdrawn, don't count.
wrong_passage_rate.outof: Out of the sources opened that week.

precision_recall.name: Precision at 10 and recall at 20
precision_recall.definition: On the held-out set of labeled queries, precision at 10 is the share of my top 10 passages that a person labeled as right, and recall at 20 is the share of the right passages that appear in my top 20. Both use only documents published before each query's date. Normalized discounted cumulative gain at 10 (nDCG at 10) is in the table beside them.
precision_recall.outof: Out of the queries in the held-out set.

rolling_coverage.name: Rolling coverage of the 8-in-10 range
rolling_coverage.definition: Of the packages that finished in the last 12 months, the share that finished inside the 8-in-10 range I gave them. A well-sized range catches about 8 in 10, so the target is 75 to 85 percent. Coverage outside it for 2 months in a row raises a retrain.
rolling_coverage.outof: Out of the packages that finished in the 12 months.

plan_accuracy.name: Plan accuracy
plan_accuracy.definition: The median number of days between a plan row's planned signing date and the actual one, early or late. I report it for plan rows dated within 14 days of a date I offered and for all other plan rows, and separately for countries not yet using Prism.
plan_accuracy.outof: Out of the plan rows with an actual date.
